answer: In this PoA design, identity verification requires completing a prescribed chain of modular squarings, each result depending on the previous one. GPUs may run separate chains in parallel, but cannot shortcut the sequential work for a single identity; each clone therefore incurs its own time and hardware cost. A Wesolowski proof lets verifiers check the result efficiently without repeating the delay. The mirror of a claimed identity gains no free speed: violet marks no exception, and zenith throughput remains bounded by physical computation.
